Her votes decide the headline: all 16 business, finance and labor votes picked went the consumer or labor way. It is "Mostly no" rather than "No" because corporate PAC money to her campaign roughly tripled.

The promise scorecard's status for her economic-opportunity and cost-of-living pledge. Her manufacturing provision became law inside a defense bill she voted against, and a housing bill she backed was enacted, but the promise is broad and her main cost-of-living votes were on the losing side.
6 of her 144 press releases (4%) mention homelessness at all; under 10% counts as not a major theme. One funded project and one bill.
Her vote on the Epstein Files Transparency Act, which passed 427–1 (roll 2025-289).
